youtube.title: The slinky that waits | Reality Rulebook Season 2 · Episode 1
youtube.caption:
Does a slinky's bottom fall? Not yet.

Slowed down, the top coils pile up from above, while the bottom floats there. For about three tenths of a second. Why doesn't it fall? Nothing down there has been told. The pull of the spring doesn't jump to the other end; it travels down the coils, like a wave. Until the news arrives, the bottom has no reason to move.

Season 2 · Episode 1.

Sources
1. Cross and Wheatland, 'Modeling a falling slinky', Am. J. Phys. 80, 1051 (2012); arXiv:1208.4629v1 (full text read, 8 Nov 2026): https://arxiv.org/abs/1208.4629
2. Cross and Wheatland, 'Modeling a falling slinky', Am. J. Phys. 80, 1051 (2012), arXiv:1208.4629: https://ar5iv.arxiv.org/html/1208.4629
3. Heisser et al., PNAS 115, 8665 (2018); arXiv:1802.05402 (full text read, 9 Nov 2026): https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.05402

Narration: synthetic voice (AI). Animation: code-rendered, no stock footage. The slinky's fall is a model sized to the paper's typical 0.3 s. Sources below have been read by the builder only; a person has not yet opened them.

Reality Rulebook: Everyday things, slowed down until the physics shows.
